messages.text:
"Build a fully playable 2D mobile tower defense game called LAST STAND.

Platform: Android and mobile browsers. Portrait orientation (9:16).

GAMEPLAY:
Enemies follow a winding path toward the player's base. The player builds defensive towers beside the path to eliminate enemies before they reach the base.

TOWERS:

- Machine Gun: fast attacks, low damage.
- Sniper: slow attacks, high damage and long range.
- Cannon: area damage against groups.
- Ice Tower: slows enemy movement.

ENEMIES:

- Basic enemy.
- Fast enemy.
- Armored enemy.
- Heavy boss enemy.

MECHANICS:

- Enemies spawn in waves and follow the path.
- Towers automatically detect and attack enemies in range.
- Defeated enemies reward coins.
- Spend coins to build and upgrade towers.
- Each enemy reaching the base reduces its health.
- The game ends when base health reaches zero.
- Win by surviving all waves.

FEATURES:

- 10 progressively harder waves.
- Tower placement and upgrade menus.
- Enemy health bars.
- Base health indicator.
- Coin counter.
- Wave counter.
- Pause and speed controls.
- Victory and defeat screens.
- Restart button.

VISUAL STYLE:
Colorful polished 2D graphics, detailed battlefield, readable tower designs, smooth projectiles, explosions and satisfying effects.

IMPORTANT:
Implement actual tower targeting, projectile movement, enemy pathfinding, collision/damage, wave progression and resource management.

All controls must work on mobile touchscreens. Build a real playable game, not a mockup. Do not use keyboard-dependent controls.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.text:
"Build a fully playable 2D mobile tower defense game called LAST STAND.

Platform: Android and mobile browsers. Portrait orientation (9:16).

GAMEPLAY:
Enemies follow a winding path toward the player's base. The player builds defensive towers beside the path to eliminate enemies before they reach the base.

TOWERS:

- Machine Gun: fast attacks, low damage.
- Sniper: slow attacks, high damage and long range.
- Cannon: area damage against groups.
- Ice Tower: slows enemy movement.

ENEMIES:

- Basic enemy.
- Fast enemy.
- Armored enemy.
- Heavy boss enemy.

MECHANICS:

- Enemies spawn in waves and follow the path.
- Towers automatically detect and attack enemies in range.
- Defeated enemies reward coins.
- Spend coins to build and upgrade towers.
- Each enemy reaching the base reduces its health.
- The game ends when base health reaches zero.
- Win by surviving all waves.

FEATURES:

- 10 progressively harder waves.
- Tower placement and upgrade menus.
- Enemy health bars.
- Base health indicator.
- Coin counter.
- Wave counter.
- Pause and speed controls.
- Victory and defeat screens.
- Restart button.

VISUAL STYLE:
Colorful polished 2D graphics, detailed battlefield, readable tower designs, smooth projectiles, explosions and satisfying effects.

IMPORTANT:
Implement actual tower targeting, projectile movement, enemy pathfinding, collision/damage, wave progression and resource management.

All controls must work on mobile touchscreens. Build a real playable game, not a mockup. Do not use keyboard-dependent controls.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile tower defense game called LAST STAND for Android and mobile browsers, in portrait orientation.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, targeting/projectiles/damage, path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, victory/defeat, pause and speed controls, and restart.
- Make all controls work with mobile touchscreens; do not rely on keyboard controls.
- Deliver a polished, colorful 2D game rather than a mockup.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module with a separate configuration module.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside the path.
- Balance-check the simulation with a headless harness.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added tower, enemy, wave, and balance configuration in `js/config.js`.
- Added simulation in `js/game.js`: path layout and following, tower placement/upgrades/selling, targeting, projectiles, damage, armor, slow effects, rewards, wave progression, and win/defeat states.
- Added `js/package.json` with `"type": "module"`.
- Added `sim/balance.mjs`; `node sim/balance.mjs` ran five strategies, each reaching victory in the harness.
- Changes are uncommitted.

### Active
- Build the game’s HTML/CSS interface, canvas renderer, touch interaction, menus, pause/speed controls, and effects.
- Run the app and check its appearance and playable controls on mobile and desktop.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create the page structure and responsive styling for the portrait game, HUD, tower selection, upgrade panel, and end screens.
2. Implement canvas rendering and touch interactions wired to `Game`.
3. Run the project, test the full play loop and controls, and fix any simulation or presentation issues.
4. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation, `Game`, `Tower`, and `Enemy`.
- `js/config.js`: Game settings, tower/enemy definitions, wave lists.
- `js/package.json`: Enables ES modules for the simulation.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless strategy and balance harness.

## Important Context
- The balance harness reports all five tested strategies reaching wave 10 victory.
- Tower damage accounting was corrected to pass `towerId` through projectile hits.
- The project currently has no `index.html` or game UI/renderer implementation.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable portrait mobile tower defense game called LAST STAND for Android and mobile browsers.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, combat and path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, pause/speed controls, victory/defeat, and restart.
- Ensure all controls work with touchscreens; deliver a polished, colorful 2D game.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module with separate configuration and a canvas-based interface.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added tower, enemy, wave, and balance configuration in `js/config.js`.
- Added simulation in `js/game.js`, including tower placement/upgrades/selling, targeting, projectiles, damage, path following, wave progression, rewards, and game-end states.
- Added `sim/balance.mjs`; its five tested strategies reached wave 10 victory.
- Created `index.html` and `style.css` with responsive game HUD, tower selection, upgrade panel, controls, and end screen.
- Implemented canvas battlefield rendering, touch interaction, combat effects, HUD updates, pause/speed controls, and restart in `js/main.js`.

### Active
- Validate the finished interface and game loop in a browser; fix any issues found.
- Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game and check the battlefield layout, responsive portrait display, and touch controls.
2. Test building, selecting, upgrading, selling, wave progression, pause/speed, restart, and victory/defeat.
3. Fix any runtime or presentation issues, then save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and interface elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styling.
- `js/main.js`: Canvas renderer, UI, touch interaction, and game loop.
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation.
- `js/config.js`: Game content and balance settings.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless simulation balance checks.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- UI and renderer files were just added; they have not yet been browser-tested.
- The latest `js/main.js` implementation requests animation frames and initializes the UI, but needs runtime verification.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate LAST STAND, a polished, playable portrait tower-defense game for Android and mobile browsers.
- Verify its interface and gameplay, fix issues, and capture a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, combat and path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, pause/speed controls, victory/defeat, and restart.
- Ensure all controls work with touchscreens; deliver a colorful 2D game.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module, separate configuration, and a canvas-based interface.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game configuration, simulation, and balance checks; five tested strategies reached wave 10 victory.
- Created the responsive game UI, canvas renderer, combat effects, HUD, touch interaction, controls, and end screen.
- Started the project and opened it in Chromium at `http://localhost:3000`; confirmed the page loads and the game UI renders at a 390×844 viewport.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`.

### Active
- Test building, selecting, upgrading, selling, wave progression, pause/speed, restart, and victory/defeat in the browser.
- Address any gameplay or presentation issues found in those tests.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Exercise the gameplay controls and core loop in the browser.
2. Fix any issues uncovered and recapture/inspect the current JPEG if the interface changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and interface elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styling.
- `js/main.js`: Canvas renderer, UI, touch interaction, and game loop.
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation.
- `js/config.js`: Game content and balance settings.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless balance checks.
- `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`: Current inspected screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser console showed one missing `/favicon.ico` 404; no game-related console errors were observed.
- Browser testing so far confirmed initial rendering only; gameplay interactions remain unverified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate LAST STAND, a polished, playable portrait tower-defense game for Android and mobile browsers.
- Verify its interface and gameplay, fix issues found, and capture a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, combat and path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, pause/speed controls, victory/defeat, and restart.
- Ensure all controls work with touchscreens; deliver a colorful 2D game.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module, separate configuration, and a canvas-based interface.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game configuration, simulation, and balance checks; five tested strategies reached wave 10 victory.
- Created responsive game UI, canvas renderer, combat effects, HUD, touch interaction, controls, and end screen.
- Opened the app at `http://localhost:3000` in Chromium and confirmed the page and game UI render.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`.

### Active
- Test building, selecting, upgrading, selling, wave progression, pause/speed, restart, and victory/defeat in the browser.
- Address any gameplay or presentation issues uncovered.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Exercise gameplay controls and the core loop in the browser.
2. Fix any issues found and recapture/inspect the JPEG if the interface changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and interface elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styling.
- `js/main.js`: Canvas renderer, UI, touch interaction, and game loop.
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation.
- `js/config.js`: Game content and balance settings.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless balance checks.
- `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`: Current inspected screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- Headless balance run showed all five strategies winning wave 10; two finished with reduced base health.
- Chromium is installed; an attempt to open `http://localhost:3002` failed with `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`; the app is available at `http://localhost:3000`.
- Browser console reported one missing `/favicon.ico` 404; no game-related console errors were observed.
- Browser testing so far confirmed rendering only; gameplay interactions remain unverified.

## Objective
- Build and validate LAST STAND, a polished, playable portrait tower-defense game for Android and mobile browsers.
- Verify its interface and gameplay, fix issues found, and capture a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, combat and path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, pause/speed controls, victory/defeat, and restart.
- Ensure all controls work with touchscreens; deliver a colorful 2D game.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module, separate configuration, and a canvas-based interface.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game configuration, simulation, and balance checks; five tested strategies reached wave 10 victory.
- Created responsive game UI, canvas renderer, combat effects, HUD, touch interaction, controls, and end screen.
- Confirmed in Chromium that building, selection, upgrade, sell, pause/resume, speed cycling, and wave start work.
- Verified tower placement, upgrade, and sale update the coin balance and selection panel as expected.
- Confirmed wave 1 begins spawning enemies and displays the wave banner; the paused UI state was verified.

### Active
- Finish browser checks for subsequent waves, restart, and victory/defeat; address any issues found.
- Recapture and inspect the JPEG if presentation changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for wave progression, restart, and end states.
2. Fix any issues uncovered and recapture/inspect the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and interface elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styling.
- `js/main.js`: Canvas renderer, UI, touch interaction, and game loop.
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation.
- `js/config.js`: Game content and balance settings.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless balance checks.
- `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or replace.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- `node sim/balance.mjs` showed all five strategies winning wave 10; two finished with reduced base health.
- Chromium is reachable at `http://localhost:3000`; the server had stopped during testing but was restarted successfully.
- The browser viewport was 1050×793 with the canvas centered at x≈302; pointer tests must add the canvas bounding rectangle to canvas-relative pad coordinates.
- No game-related console errors were observed in the latest checks; an earlier `/favicon.ico` request returned 404.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and validate LAST STAND, a polished, playable portrait tower-defense game for Android and mobile browsers.
- Verify gameplay and interface, fix issues found, and capture a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Implement 10 progressively harder waves, four tower types, four enemy types, combat and path following, rewards, upgrades, base health, pause/speed controls, victory/defeat, and restart.
- Ensure all controls work with touchscreens; deliver a colorful 2D game.

## Decisions
- Use a pure JavaScript simulation module, separate configuration, and a canvas-based interface.
- Use a portrait battlefield with a winding path and build slots beside it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game configuration, simulation, balance checks, responsive canvas UI, combat effects, HUD, touch interaction, controls, and end screen.
- Confirmed five headless strategies reach wave 10 victory with `node sim/balance.mjs`.
- Browser-tested building, selection, upgrade, sell, pause/resume, speed cycling, and wave start.
- Verified wave progression through all 10 waves and victory in Chromium using a simulated build strategy; result showed 192 kills and 13/20 base HP.
- Victory modal displayed with correct result statistics.

### Active
- Test restart from the victory screen, check defeat-state behavior, and recapture/inspect the current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Click “DEPLOY AGAIN” from the victory modal and verify the game resets to wave 1 prep with initial health and coins.
2. Exercise a defeat scenario and verify the defeat modal and restart.
3. Save and inspect an updated screenshot at `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and interface elements.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual styling.
- `js/main.js`: Canvas renderer, UI, touch interaction, and game loop.
- `js/game.js`: Core simulation.
- `js/config.js`: Game content and balance settings.
- `sim/balance.mjs`: Headless balance checks.
- `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg`: Existing screenshot to replace or validate.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- Chromium is reachable at `http://localhost:3000`; the server was restarted after stopping during earlier checks.
- Browser viewport was 1050×793; canvas bounds were x≈302, width≈446, height=793. Pointer tests must add the canvas bounding rectangle to canvas-relative pad coordinates.
- Test instrumentation captured the current simulation instance as `window.__lastStandTestGame`; the in-browser accelerated test reached victory.
- The previous `start.sh` invocation timed out after 120 seconds; the browser server remained available afterward.
- `screenshots/last-stand-current.jpg` was 46,479 bytes before final testing; no new capture has been made yet.
